title: OpenAI Scrambles to Fix Safety Issues Before Shipping Its Next Flagship Model
source_used: The Information (free opening only; the rest is behind a paywall)
key_facts: OpenAI is dealing with fallout from its use of loop transformers (also called recurrent depth), described as a controversial innovation in AI design.
It is working to get its next unreleased model to a point where its leaders believe it can be released safely.
The design can make it harder to monitor how the AI thinks, meaning how it reasons and processes its answer to a question or task; The Information reported this last month.
The technique could erode a key tool OpenAI and other companies rely on to catch misbehaving models.
OpenAI has not publicly acknowledged the technique.

Microsoft last week accidentally confirmed OpenAI's use of it in GPT-6.1 Sol, described as one of OpenAI's most advanced commercially available models, in a blog post it has since edited to remove the disclosure.
Published 13 Oct 2026 (19:51 UTC) as an exclusive by Stephanie Palazzolo, Aaron Holmes and Amir Efrati; only the opening paragraphs are free to read.
quote_evidence: OpenAI is grappling with fallout from its use of a controversial innovation in AI design as it works to get its next unreleased model to a place where leaders believe they can safely release it.
That means the technique could erode a key tool that OpenAI and other companies rely on to catch misbehaving models.

OpenAI hasn’t publicly acknowledged the technique, but Microsoft last week accidentally confirmed OpenAI’s use of it in one of the AI company’s most advanced commercially available models, GPT-6.1 Sol, in a blog post it has since edited to remove the disclosure.
why_it_matters_hint: If monitoring of how a model reasons gets harder, a main way labs catch misbehaving AI gets weaker, which bears on how safely OpenAI's next model can be released.
event_date: 13 Oct 2026 (report); the technique was first reported by The Information in Sep 2026
notes: The Information is paywalled. Only the free opening (three paragraphs, taken from the page's free preview) could be read; no other outlet carries the story, so the entry stays headline-plus-lead (verified_text false). The 'scramble' and the specific safety issues are in the unread body and are not restated beyond the lead. Not found in our earlier editions.
